claim.statement: The sequence likely represents p(n,4), the number of partitions of n into parts at most 4. The exact closed-form denumerant formula for this is well-known: it involves n^3/144 plus lower-order polynomial and periodic correction terms. This attempts to reconstruct that formula. Parent_4's approach was in the right family but used wrong coefficients. p(26,4) should equal 99 if this identification is correct. The known formula is floor((n+4)^3/144) with quasi-polynomial corrections.
